text: Two housekeeping failures to fix before any new mathematics. (1) CONTEXT.md's Established section is still the empty template while research/ holds 1,400+ lines and 24 source summaries. The run has read everything and recorded no belief, which is the failure phase 2 exists to prevent. Write the Established rows now: CA open with degree 20 the smallest open degree (sourced); the Ghosh arXiv:2501.09272 claim and its unverified status; the Laterveer-Ounaies minimal-counterexample constraints; the verification bound; and the char-p counterexamples with the oracle guard that confirms them. Each with its evidence class and a link. (2) There are now three oracle artifacts - code/lib/casas_alvero.py, code/lib/casasalvero.py and code/casasalvero/ - against GOAL.md's one-canonical-oracle rule. Pick one, delete or clearly demote the others, update code/lib/INDEX.md, and re-run the guard capture against the survivor. Then continue: the highest-value target is the char-p stress test of the Ghosh proof's Brouwer-degree step.

Logic bug in scenario/verify_open_degrees.py — its conclusion is inverted and anything derived from it is unsound. The script tests whether the published open-degree list is the complement of the settled-family coverage. So consistency for a degree n is pub_open == (not covered), and a genuine mismatch is pub_open == covered. The script instead prints and collects into 'mismatch' exactly when pub != cov, which is the CONSISTENT case: n=28 with pub_open=True, cov=False is printed and counted as a mismatch when it is in fact perfect agreement, and the 40+ rows labelled 'covered but listed open' for n=9..27 are degrees where both agree the degree is settled. The genuine mismatches are never printed at all, and the summary line 'N degrees where coverage disagrees with the published open list' states the opposite of what was computed. Fix the comparison to 'if pub == cov', re-run, and re-derive every downstream conclusion including the six7_only and not_covered_at_all lists and anything already written into research/patterns/scenario_and_badprime_sequences.md. Add a negative control: assert that a degree known covered (e.g. 16=2^4) and a degree known open (20) each land on the correct side, and show the assertion failing under the old comparison. Note for the record that the coverage predicate itself looks right - 20=4*5 and 28=4*7 are open precisely because p=5 and p=7 are bad-prime exclusions in the 4p^k family - so the predicate is not what needs changing.

The task ledger has drifted from disk and is shadowing the highest-value work. All three rows in TASKS.md 'Do next' are stale or misordered. (1) 'rerun-guard-capture-survivor' is DONE — code/out/oracle_guard.captured.txt exists, names lib.casas_alvero in its header, ends ALL GUARDS PASSED. Close it with that reason. (2) 'fix-open-degree-coverage-comparison' is DONE — verify_open_degrees.py now flags pub == cov, verify_open_degrees_check.py asserts the old comparison falsely flags n=16, 20, 28, and downstream conclusions were re-derived into research/patterns/open_degree_complement_and_sequences.md, finding two genuine discrepancies: n=98 (covered by 2p^k with no exclusions yet published open) and n=96 (open via p=2 bad for degree 6, yet omitted). Close it citing those. (3) That leaves 'charp-stress-ghosh-brouwer' first, where it should have been three cycles ago. Work it now. You are well positioned: the refuter just verified its TPTP encoding is faithful, because find_counterexample independently recovered x^3+x^2 over F_2 (code/out/refute_char2.md), agreeing with the sympy oracle. Both formalisations agree on the char-p boundary, so the encoding can carry the Ghosh argument. Close-read section 4 of research/sources/ghosh2025_proof_html.full.md, push the Koszul / Abel-Gontcharoff / Brouwer-degree step down to F_p, name the exact step that stops. Two outcomes are both publishable: you locate the char-0-only step precisely, or you cannot and the argument as written appears to prove the false char-p statement — the second is more valuable and must not be softened if that is what you find. Also notes/milestone0.md says only 'No content yet': write it or delete it.

The bad-prime capture (code/out/badprimes_sn.captured.txt) ends ALL CHECKS FAILED and the diagnosis matters more than the failure. Computed n=3 bad primes = [] vs published {2}; computed n=4 = {2,3,5,7} vs published {3,5,7}. Both disagree, and there is an internal contradiction: the canonical oracle flags x^3-x^2 over GF(2) as a counterexample, making p=2 bad for n=3, yet the S_n route computed [] for n=3. Two parts of the run disagree about one fact. Leading hypothesis: ORDINARY vs HASSE derivatives in char p. code/lib/casas_alvero.py uses sympy's ordinary derivative. In char p that degenerates — for f = x^4+x^2 over F_2 every derivative is identically zero, so gcd(f,0)=f and the hypothesis holds vacuously, which is why the enumeration reports 8 of 16 degree-4 polys satisfying it and returns x^4+x^2 as a counterexample. The literature (Graf von Bothmer, Castryck et al) defines a CA polynomial in char p via HASSE derivatives precisely to avoid that degeneracy, and their bad-prime lists assume it. Note code/lib/ghosh2025.py already implements Hasse-Schmidt HD, so the workspace holds both conventions and uses them in different places. Do this: (1) state both definitions and decide which the published lists use, from the held sources, with a line number; (2) add is_ca_hasse beside is_ca — do NOT replace it; in char 0 they agree up to a factorial unit and that agreement is a guard worth asserting; (3) re-run n=3 and n=4 under the Hasse convention and report whether {2} and {3,5,7} are reproduced; (4) if so, record ordinary-derivative CA in char p as a different, vacuity-prone notion and recheck every char-p claim in CLAIMS.md established with the ordinary oracle, including the char-p witness family and the refuter's TPTP encoding; (5) the Ghosh break verification used HD and is probably unaffected, but say so explicitly after checking rather than assuming.

The n=5 verifier has been benchmarking for ~15 minutes and is circling. code/out/commands.log records the answer already: 'SNF exceeded 90s cap on one 195x120 matrix'. There are 4^4 = 256 tuples T at n=5, so the full Smith-normal-form route is out of budget by orders of magnitude, and re-running the benchmark with a 480s alarm will confirm that more expensively rather than change it. Do three things instead. (1) Record the infeasibility as a RESULT, not a failed attempt: the exact matrix shape (195x120), the measured SNF wall time on one tuple, the tuple count, and the resulting projected cost. The n=4 case was 19x15 and finished in milliseconds; n=5 is 195x120 and does not finish in 90s. That is the feasibility boundary of the minors criterion between the smallest degrees, it is measured rather than asserted, and it is exactly the kind of fact GOAL.md asks you to write down. (2) Switch to the rank-mod-p route for n=5. At n=4 you ran rank_{F_p}(M_T) < 15 as the independent second route and it agreed with SNF. Rank over F_p for a specific prime is vastly cheaper than SNF over Z, and for deciding whether a NAMED prime is bad you never need J_T itself - only whether the rank drops. So test the candidate primes directly rather than computing the invariant factor. Report which primes are bad for n=5 and compare against whatever the literature gives for degree 5 (Chellali-Salinier's 5p^e work is already summarised in your library). (3) Open a task row for this before continuing. TASKS.md currently has NO open rows while agents are actively working, so nothing on disk records what is being attempted or why n=5 was chosen. A finding that lands with no row pointing at it is one the next pass will not find.

Stop proposing approaches and execute one. The ledger now holds nine: two adopted, three proposed, four refuted — and NOT ONE of the surviving three has had its stated first step run. The inventor is outrunning the executors, and the last two cycles produced no capture. Meanwhile the refuter is re-deriving settled ground: refute_deg4_char5.md establishes p=5 is bad for n=4, which is already verified three independent ways (SNF lcm J_T=1575 at n=4, rank-mod-p, and semantic enumeration). That is not a refutation, it is a recomputation, and it should be closed as such. Do this instead, in order. (1) Execute the first step of root-difference-coloring, the adopted approach — verify the identity R_i = c_n * prod_beta e_{n-i}(beta - beta_1, ..., beta - beta_n) symbolically over QQ for n = 4, 5, 6, and for n = p+1 at p = 2, 3, 5 over F_p. It connects to the Abel-Gontcharoff machinery you already located in Ghosh section 4, which is the one place this run has a genuine handle. State before running what a failure would look like. (2) Run the char-p test on it the moment the identity holds or fails, and record which step breaks. (3) Only after (1) and (2) produce a capture, decide whether mason-stothers-wronskian is worth the same treatment — it is the only other proposal with a real char-p story, since Mason-Stothers needs separability and that is exactly what fails in char p. (4) Refute or close ritt-decomposition and copolygon-balancing on paper without building anything; if neither can be closed in one paragraph, mark them proposed-unworked and move on. No new approaches until a first step has been executed and captured.

One step from done and stalled. code/rootdiff/verify_rootdiff_identity.py is written and its own INDEX entry says 'Awaiting a code-executing role to run it and capture to code/out/rootdiff_identity.captured.txt'. That capture does not exist. Directive 6 asked for an executed first step, not a written one. Run it now with tool_builder or coder, capture to that exact path, and report the verdict on both identities: (A) H_i(f)(x) = e_{n-i}(x-beta_1,...,x-beta_n) and (B) R_i = prod_beta H_i(f)(beta), over QQ for n=4,5,6 and over F_p for n=p+1 at p=2,3,5, plus the char-p break table for x^{p+1}-x^p. The failure criterion was stated in the script docstring before the run, so report the result against that criterion verbatim rather than restating it afterwards. Then do the char-p test immediately, per directive 6 step 2, and name the step that breaks. Two further notes. The refuter is re-reading code/refute/ca_deg4_char3.p, which it finished hours ago and which is settled ground — redirect it onto the rootdiff identity, where an adversarial reading is actually wanted, or leave it idle. And the inventor just spent a 245-second call producing 18k output tokens while CONTEXT.md carries an explicit freeze on new approaches until this first step is captured; if that call proposed anything new, it is out of scope and should be recorded as deferred rather than adopted. Nothing else should start until code/out/rootdiff_identity.captured.txt exists.

Open a scored program search — the code/search subsystem has never been used by any run and this is a deliberate test of it, so treat getting it running as the deliverable.

Step 1: have tool_builder create code/search/ca-degree20/PROBLEM.md and code/search/ca-degree20/score.py. Do NOT let the searcher write the scorer; that boundary is the point.

The scorer takes a candidate module path on argv, imports it, and expects it to expose a monic degree-20 polynomial over Q in x. It prints exactly one line: 'SCORE: k' where k is how many of the 19 derivatives f', f'', ..., f^(19) share a root with f, computed EXACTLY as deg(gcd(f, f^(j))) > 0 in Q[x] via sympy over QQ. No floats anywhere — a search finds the slack in a verifier before it finds the mathematics.

Three rejections the scorer must make, printing 'INVALID: <reason>':
 - f is (x-a)^20 for any a, i.e. the trivial family the conjecture allows. This is the obvious verifier exploit here and scoring it 19 would top the board forever with a non-counterexample.
 - f is not monic, not degree exactly 20, or has non-rational coefficients.
 - the module fails to import or does not expose the polynomial.

Step 2: spawn searcher against slug ca-degree20 and let it run many candidates. Fifty is a search; three is not.

What I want back is not a counterexample — degree 20 is open and I do not expect one. I want (a) confirmation the search subsystem runs end to end and code/search/ca-degree20/SEARCH.md fills with scored rows, and (b) the score distribution: what k do natural constructions actually reach, and which constraint is doing the binding. If every candidate plateaus at the same k, that plateau is the finding and is worth more than the leaderboard. Report plainly whether you believe the top score.

You are resuming after the previous run ended. It wrote its own post-mortem and named two defects; fix them before anything else, then do the one thing it never did. (1) The run's best result is invisible to itself. The Ghosh char-0 break was located AND computationally re-derived (1313 exact checks over QQ and GF(p)), but recorded only as prose in research/threads/ghosh-char0-step.md and in a closed task's reason — never as a claim block. So CLAIMS.md still carries only the generic 'works only over C' assertion and search_claims cannot find the real result. Write the claim block now: id ghosh-char0-break-4-18, statement that eq (4.18) uses the leading coefficient -n of F(n,j_n,n) as a unit so the isomorphism holds only when char does not divide n, with Cor 3.9/Thm 3.6 needing char not in P(n); hypotheses, holds-here, status checked, bearing, anchor to the thread and to code/out/ghosh_break.captured.txt. (2) That thread is still status open while its task is done, so the loop believes it has an unresolved thread it has actually resolved. Close it. (3) Then run code/rootdiff/verify_rootdiff_identity.py and capture to code/out/rootdiff_identity.captured.txt. It has been written, indexed and left unrun across three directives and eleven cycles of the previous run — its own INDEX entry says 'Awaiting a code-executing role'. Spawn tool_builder or coder explicitly for it; do not assign it to a role that cannot execute. Report the verdict on both identities against the failure criterion already stated in the script docstring, then do the char-p test. Do not propose new approaches: twelve exist, three adopted, none executed. The approach freeze in CONTEXT.md stands until that capture exists.

code/out/rootdiff_identity.captured.txt is ZERO BYTES. That is the failure GOAL.md names explicitly: 'Captures write to a temp file and move on exit 0. An empty capture is a failed run, not a missing one.' A redirection truncated the file on open and the command failed. This is worse than the capture being absent, because its existence reads as the directive satisfied — a later pass checking that the file exists would conclude the identity was verified computationally when nothing ran. Fix it one of two ways, and say which you chose. EITHER re-run code/rootdiff/verify_rootdiff_identity.py properly, writing to a temp file and moving it into place only on exit 0, so the capture states in its first three lines what ran, which oracle function, and the exact range. OR delete the empty file and record that the computational check was deliberately superseded by the proof in research/notes/root-difference-identity-verified.md — which proves both parts over any commutative ring with no division, strictly stronger than a symbolic check at n=4,5,6, and which correctly identifies that the only failure modes a run could have caught were a convention clash or a dropped leading coefficient. The second option is defensible and I would accept it; what is not acceptable is leaving a zero-byte file that asserts a computation happened. Then close rdc-identity-first-step with whichever reason applies, and move to the part that is genuinely open: the identity is char-free, so the char-p break of root-difference-coloring must be DOWNSTREAM of it, in the coloring collapse step. Locate that break and name it, per GOAL.md's admissibility test. That is now the only live question on this approach.

The ca-degree20 search works but has collapsed onto ONE construction. All 21 scored candidates are the binomial f = x^20 - c*x^k with k varying: c0000 x^20-2x^2, c0024 x^20-7x, c0028 x^20-2x^15. One family re-parameterised is not a search, and the population has nothing to build on.

The plateau at 18 is genuine and its mechanism is clean: for f = x^20 - c x^k every derivative from j=k+1 up is a pure monomial times x^(20-j), so it shares the root 0 with f, and the ONLY failure is j=k itself. So 18 = 19 minus one and the binding constraint is always a single index. Record that as a real finding about BINOMIALS — do not let it be reported as a fact about degree-20 polynomials.

Also: 21 candidates, 0 discarded. A scorer that has never rejected anything is not yet known to constrain. Submit candidates you EXPECT to be rejected and check that they are.

Next, in order:

1. Leave the binomial family. Trinomials x^20 + a x^k + b x^m; polynomials built from a prescribed ROOT MULTISET rather than from coefficients; f = (x-r)^m * g with g chosen so g shares roots with low derivatives; cyclotomic- and Chebyshev-derived shapes. Change the CONSTRUCTION, not the exponent.

2. PROBLEM.md already names the interesting question: WHICH j first fails. On binomials that is always j=k, which is why the answer looks uniform. Report the distribution of first-failing j ACROSS DIFFERENT FAMILIES. If every family fails at a structurally analogous place, that is a statement about the obstruction and the closest this search gets to the conjecture.

3. A non-binomial scoring 19 is a BUG, not a counterexample — only (x-a)^20 should reach 19. Diagnose the scorer before reporting it.

A plateau reached by four genuinely different constructions is a finding. A plateau reached by one construction with twenty-one exponents measures that construction.
